articles.title_orig: Helen Haines has lost both legs after alleged attack but ‘her heart and mind are in good shape’, husband says
articles.title_zh: Helen Haines has lost both legs after alleged attack but ‘her heart and mind are in good shape’, husband says
articles.content_orig:
Haines is in stable condition. Surgeons tried to save her right leg but both have now been amputated due to injuries
Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast
The independent MP Helen Haines has lost both legs but remains in a stable condition, two days after an alleged targeted attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria.
Haines, the federal MP for Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was struck by a car in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon. Surgeons were trying to save her right leg on Tuesday, but both legs had to be amputated due to the seriousness of her injuries.
Her husband, Phil Haines, provided an update on his wife’s condition at Melbourne’s Alfred hospital late on Wednesday afternoon.
Composed and clear, he said his wife had survived a “horrendous incident” and faced a long road to recovery.
“The good news in all this is Helen is alive and she’s stable,” he said.
“That is the most important thing for our family. And I think when we reflect and talk about and think about Helen, the two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind.
“Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person. Incredibly supportive of all around her – her family, her community, anybody she comes across. And her mind. She has the sharpest intellect.”
Phil Haines described his wife, 65, as a fighter. The pair have been married for nearly 40 years and have three children and two grandchildren. He became emotional for a moment at the end of the statement, reflecting on his wife’s strength.
“She is a determined person who will do her best with our support and love to recover, and that is what we hope for,” he said.
“We are grateful at this stage that both her heart and her mind are in good shape.”
Haines asked for donations to Save the Children as his wife recovers. A special appeal has been launched by the charity.
Police allege Monday’s attack was targeted, and have charged Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official.
Nugent faced Wangaratta magistrates court earlier on Wednesday.
Phil Haines was joined by the governor general, Sam Mostyn. Mostyn said she had relayed news of the incident to King Charles and praised Helen Haines’s work as a local representative, including her commitment to improving the standards of public discourse in Australia.
“This violent attack on a much loved and respected sitting member of our federal parliament must be a moment for us to pause and to choose to be better,” she said.
“We’ve got to hope that that beautiful heart, that beautiful mind will be strengthened every day by our support and our commitment to be more like Helen as part of this great democracy.”
Anthony Albanese and politicians from across federal parliament have expressed shock and anger at the alleged attack on Haines.
The incident has sparked calls for changes to politicians’ safety, with security services including the Australian federal police and Asio briefing MPs on the current landscape on Wednesday.
Speaking at a vigil in Wodonga on Wednesday evening, Cathy McGowan, who held the seat of Indi before Haines, paid tribute to her friend.
“There is another level of grief, different and deeper from the actual violence, from the sorrow, the shame and the hurt,” she said.
“It’s about Helen in her role as our elected representative. In attacking her, we intuit that this is an attack on our political system, on our democracy, and especially so for all the supporters who did the democracy work getting Helen elected.”
McGowan called for the upcoming Victorian state election campaign to be conducted in a positive and constructive way. Voters go to the polls next month.
The community could not let violence win, McGowan implored.
“That we ensure the legacy of this attack on Helen will be a stronger, more vibrant and effective democracy, and from a personal perspective, all candidates and especially women, know they can run for office and be safe.”

articles.title_orig: Musk pledges $10bn in SpaceX shares for US children: Who really gains?
articles.title_zh: Musk pledges $10bn in SpaceX shares for US children: Who really gains?
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk has pledged to give one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year – a gift that could be worth more than $10bn.
“This will be the first of many,” the world’s richest man wrote on X on Monday.
About 73 million children under 18 live in the US, according to US Census Bureau data.
At Friday’s closing price of $146.03, the pledge would be worth about $10.7bn.
President Donald Trump thanked Musk on his Truth Social platform, and claimed the shares would be given to children “through TRUMP ACCOUNTS”, the tax-friendly investment accounts for children created under his signature tax and spending law last year.
The pledge comes two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.
Musk is the biggest known donor in the run-up to those elections, having given more than $276m to Republican groups since July.
Musk has not said which children will qualify, when the shares will be handed over, or how.
So how might the giveaway work, and who stands to gain?
Here’s what you need to know:
SpaceX, the world’s seventh-largest company, began trading on the Nasdaq in June at an initial public offering price of $135 per share. That price has been volatile. SpaceX shares have fallen 35.3 percent since peaking days after the listing.
The shares are currently trading at around $146 a share. Every $1 move in the share price will change the gift’s value by about $73m.
Musk owns 4.8 billion shares in SpaceX outright, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in August.
Including unvested awards and stock options, his stake rises to about 6.4 billion shares, or 48.4 percent of the company.
Giving away 73 million shares would reduce his outright holding by about 1.5 percent, barely affecting his control of the company. That’s because his voting power, which is currently about 82 percent because SpaceX has two classes of shares, would fall by only 0.1 percentage points, according to a Bloomberg Opinion calculation.
It would be the largest single gift linked to Trump accounts so far.
Trump said the shares would be held in Trump accounts, and Musk thanked Brad Gerstner, the tech investor behind the accounts, for “helping enable this”.
Nearly 70 million Trump accounts have been opened, one for every child under 18 with a Social Security number, according to the White House. Investments held in Trump accounts can roll up with tax deferred until they are withdrawn when a child turns 18. Alternatively, they can be rolled into a tax-friendly IRA – a retirement account for adults – and continue with the tax-friendly status.
Under Treasury rules published on September 30, donors can now gift individual company stock to children via the accounts. Families and friends making regular contributions to a child’s Trump account are limited to investing low-risk index funds.
Families cannot refuse the shares on behalf of their children and generally cannot sell them for five years, or until the end of the year the child turns 17 if that comes sooner.
Musk cannot sell or trade most of his SpaceX shares until June 2027, the Wall Street Journal reported.
The accounts carry the president’s name, and Trump has tied himself closely to the gift.
He thanked Musk on Truth Social, saying the pledge was “exactly what was envisioned when we created TRUMP ACCOUNTS”.
The White House has presented the accounts as a signature achievement of Trump’s tax law, noting that “every single Democrat voted against” the legislation.
The pledge also marks a public reconciliation. Musk and Trump fell out in 2025 over Trump’s tax-and-spending bill, a rift Trump later called a “little dispute”.
Children will be gaining a share for free, but the gift could also save Musk money.
Donors who give appreciated stock to charity avoid capital gains tax and can usually claim a deduction, the US broadcaster CNBC reported.
As SpaceX’s founder, Musk paid very little for his shares, and selling $10.7bn of them could mean a tax bill of up to about $2.5bn.
It is “a popular practice for particularly high-income taxpayers that would otherwise be paying a high rate”, Will McBride, chief economist at the Tax Foundation, told the broadcaster in May.
Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, told Inc. magazine that millions of shareholders unable to sell would also have an interest in SpaceX’s success and in “minimising its regulatory burdens”.
For Mitchell Downey, an economist at Stockholm University’s Institute for International Economic Studies who studies political influence in the US, the more striking part of the pledge is what he called “the horseshoe aspect of this” – the idea that right-wing and left-wing policies can curve around and meet.
For decades, progressives have backed the concept of Child Development Accounts, investment accounts for every newborn designed to reduce inequality in wealth, he said. The idea was associated with groups such as the Democracy Collaborative but struggled to gain federal support. Now the idea may become more mainstream as a result of Musk’s gift and Trump accounts.
“It always felt like it might be out of reach,” Downey said. “But I don’t see how Musk’s proposal would be possible without building some infrastructure like this.”
The pledge comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the two houses of Congress. All seats in the House of Representatives and one-third of the Senate are up for re-election.
Trump’s approval rating has meanwhile fallen to a record low of 33 percent, according to a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll, with many political observers expecting to see the Republicans lose seats to the Democratic Party as a result.
Musk, who campaigned with Trump in 2024 and spearheaded the president’s Department of Government Efficiency initiative to reduce the size of the federal workforce, has contributed heavily to Republican candidates in advance of the midterm elections.
Downey said he does not believe the pledge raises legal concerns.
“Individuals are allowed to spend their money in support of a politician,” he told Al Jazeera. “The law only gets violated when either it isn’t publicly reported, or it is part of an explicit and documented quid-pro-quo.”
But he said it does raise ethical concerns, though not ones unique to Musk’s approach.
Those concerns relate to “the outsized role that external donors play in US elections”, Downey said. In his view, they apply much like when someone spends heavily on television advertisements for a candidate.
Downey said the precedent was “hard to assess”.
Because Musk is the richest person in modern history, he said, it is perhaps unsurprising that he is “doing something that involves more money than other very rich people have done”.
He pointed to the Gates Foundation’s spending over the past three decades as “a different type of ‘gift to the public’”. The difference, he said, is that the Gates Foundation focuses funding on health crises in countries in Africa and South Asia – not on voters in the US.
Last year, Gates pledged to “give away virtually all my wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next 20 years to the cause of saving and improving lives around the world”.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Are Exploring a Merger
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together .
Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes."
The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.
With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion) and SpaceX at $2 trillion, a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.
Any deal would also need shareholder backing. But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.
"In my opinion, 100%. It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, chief technology advisor at market research firm The Futurum Group.
The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.
Musk, chief executive of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.
Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.
The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.
Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.
But the merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, with half of Tesla's needed to back the deal, a threshold even Musk described as "quite a high hurdle".
Musk, as boss of both companies, cannot participate in shareholder discussions.
Even so, Musk, a key shareholder of Tesla, will likely get his way in the next few years, said investment analyst Dan Sheehan from Telos Wealth Advisors.
He believes shareholders will back the deal as the technology the companies develop complement each other, Sheehan said.
But the merger would mean that Tesla shareholders will likely hold a "smaller slice of a much larger and more complex business," he added.
"There's no real precedent for how a public company like Tesla gets priced in this," Sheehan said.
SpaceX shares rose 8% in after hours trading while shares of Tesla climbed by 2%.
Experts told the BBC that Tesla drivers are unlikely to see much drastic change in the near term, even if the two companies combine.
In fact, vehicles seem almost like "an afterthought", overshadowed by the potential to combine the Tesla and SpaceX's tech capabilities, Nicholson said.
Changes are already underway at Tesla. The carmaker said earlier this year that it would prioritise its best-selling Model Y and Model 3, shifting focus away from less popular models .
Tesla also started using a manufacturing plant in California to produce humanoid robots, known as Optimus.
Pairing Tesla's self-driving technology and robotics with SpaceX's AI and satellite network could result in more capable vehicles, Sheehan said.
"The question is how much priority cars get inside a company increasingly driven by AI infrastructure," he added.
The recent Roadster showcase suggests SpaceX technology could be pulled into future Tesla products, which could attract more customers, said Tu Le, the founder of advisory firm Sino Auto Insights.
The Cybertruck-maker faces intense competition from Chinese carmakers like BYD, which overtook Tesla as the world's biggest EV maker in January.
The biggest winner is probably Musk - the world's richest man who also became the world's first trillionaire earlier this year.
The merger would give Musk greater voting control over the combined company than he currently has at Tesla, a factor the special committee assessing the deal would have to consider.
A single company makes it easier for Musk to run his AI strategy the way he wants, Sheehan said.
"The deal itself doesn't add to Musk's wealth, but it concentrates it further in one stock," he said.
However, the merger could attract scrutiny over Musk, already a polarising figure in the US, Nicholson said.
The move could also face more regulatory pressure if Democrats - many of whom have been critical of Musk - win more seats in the US midterm elections next month.
Shareholders have backed Musk's desires before. Last year, Tesla investors approved an unprecedented compensation package for Musk valued around $1tn .
"I honestly don't think Musk will be keeping track of what the merger will do for his wealth," Nicholson said.
The deal also brings Musk closer to what Nicholson says is "his mission in life": colonising Mars.

articles.title_orig: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
articles.title_zh: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
articles.content_orig:
Internet security and web administration teams around the world are scrambling to prevent widespread disaster. On Wednesday, the developers behind the much-used PHP programming language released emergency security updates designed to fix critical flaws that could be exploited to allow attackers to gain dangerous remote control of victim systems.
The PHP Foundation detailed the two critical vulnerabilities— CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 —which impact “all PHP installations serving web requests” going back to PHP version 5, released in July 2004. However, only PHP 8.2 and newer are still supported and will receive patches, according to the alert. The PHP Foundation noted, though, that some PHP distributions and third-party vendors still produce legacy fixes. The caveat is significant, because ubiquitous and foundational web layers like PHP can persist forgotten and un-updated in historic internet infrastructure.
“There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice,” the PHP Foundation wrote in its advisories. Security experts warn of the potential dire consequences of overlooking unpatched systems.
“This is not a drill,” says Lukasz Olejnik, an independent security consultant and visiting senior research fellow at King’s College London. Since its development in the 1990s, PHP has evolved into an essential scripting language for web development and is used across vast swaths of the internet in websites and software. Everything from publishing systems like WordPress and Drupal to e-commerce platforms like Adobe’s Magento are built on PHP.
Olejnik likens the widespread use of the programming language to critical infrastructure.
“The impact is enormous,” he says of PHP’s security flaws, adding that millions of systems could be impacted. “Especially if attackers would turn to exploiting these vulnerabilities fast. Worst case is wormable malware affecting big chunks of the internet.”
The overriding fear for security teams and developers is that malicious hackers could quickly jump upon the vulnerabilities and begin exploiting deployments before they are fixed. Internet infrastructure company Cloudflare reported it was “seeing early attacks emerging” before the PHP Foundation had detailed the vulnerabilities and released fixes. “We expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release,” security firm Sansec wrote ahead of the fixes, which were released just before 10 am ET on Wednesday.
“Most of the web runs on PHP and this bug is in a file upload interface that’s like a front door with no lock,” says longtime security and compliance consultant Davi Ottenheimer. “An attacker does not need to know which site they are hitting or even the actual software it runs. They send one crafted upload to any server they can find, and that is the entire attack.”
Ahead of the updated versions of PHP becoming available, some organizations took their websites offline as a precautionary measure. Multiple sites belonging to the Finnish government, including the National Land Survey, were inaccessible, according to reports . French government websites and the Port of Rotterdam’s website were also offline, according to Reuters .
“Everybody should patch immediately, exploitation may happen very fast and at a scale,” says Olejnik. “AI makes exploiting such vulnerabilities of immediate importance. Like, indeed, a minute or so.”
Security company Wiz, which is owned by Google, claimed its researchers discovered the vulnerabilities in PHP partially using AI tools, while OpenAI and security firm Calif also say they independently discovered the issues and worked together. Dubbing an exploitation demonstration php2shell , the Wiz researchers write that in some cases the vulnerabilities can be exploited “fairly easily.”
“The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory,” Wiz writes in its research. “That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.”
Details of the upcoming vulnerabilities first appeared from the maintainers behind PHP on October 20. In a short post on the PHP website, the PHP Foundation wrote it was giving “advance notice” of the security flaws and upcoming release of the fixes. While omitting specific details about the vulnerabilities or the versions impacted, it said both flaws are considered to have a “critical” 9.2 score out of 10 on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS).
“We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild,” the security warning on the PHP site said ahead of Wednesday’s release. According to reports from Bleeping Computer and Ars Technica , some details about the vulnerabilities may have leaked before they were due to officially be published.
The early warning from the PHP Foundation may have given some developers, security teams, and companies enough of a heads up to start preparing to update systems using PHP. Ahead of the details being published, warnings from the EU’s Computer Emergency Response Team (EU-CERT) and Australia's cybersecurity agency said IT teams should be prepared to update their systems as soon as possible, with the potential for websites to be taken offline while fixes are applied.
Similarly, the UK’s National Cyber Security Center (NCSC), published an alert saying organizations should “prepare for immediate updating of systems” using PHP. “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organizations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated,” the agency wrote online.
The NCSC advises that organizations and businesses should identify systems running PHP across their tech infrastructure. There should be a particular focus on systems using PHP that are connected to the internet, including monitoring them for any potential exploitation. The next step is applying PHP updates as they are available and monitoring for updates from software companies as they may use PHP within their apps or services.
“If you find signs of compromise, isolate the system, preserve your web server and PHP logs, and report it to your local FBI field office,” Brett Leatherman, the FBI’s cyber assistant director posted online. “Those reports help us identify the actors involved and warn other organizations before they become victims.”

articles.title_orig: Apple Stores Will Have 'Limited' Availability of iPhone Duo for Walk-In Customers
articles.title_zh: Apple Stores Will Have 'Limited' Availability of iPhone Duo for Walk-In Customers
articles.content_orig:
It’s a little hard to review the iPhone Duo. I’ve been toting Apple’s first folding smartphone for the past week, and several apps I’ve tried to open on the sprawling 7.6-inch screen look awful. Thick, black bars on the sides, with a phone-sized app in the middle of this tablet-like display. But you likely won’t encounter this problem once the Duo is in your hands.
In the past day, a handful of apps I use regularly updated to add full support for the iPhone Duo’s screen sizes and vertical user interface elements. Instagram, Threads, Slack, and even the Google app now have navigational icons on the right rail instead of the bottom center, and the app content is better laid out to make use of the larger screen.
Developers need to target the iOS 27.1 software development kit (SDK) for full Duo compatibility. That will take some time. But it is a little maddening that some app developers, who for years have never seemed to care about optimizing their app for Android folding phones , are so quick to embrace Apple’s fold. Slack, for example, never offered the two-pane view of its desktop app in the Android version, but it’s on the Duo. C’est la vie. Hopefully, Apple’s entry into foldables will result in a “rising tide lifts all boats” situation and Android fold lovers will get to enjoy those optimizations.
The iPhone Duo’s Standby mode turns on when the phone is propped up via a kickstand.
The iPhone Duo arrives seven years after Samsung’s first Galaxy Fold . In Apple tradition, its first entry into an existing category feels fully mature; the Duo has significantly less jank than the first few generations of its Android counterparts . The infamous crease—where the phone folds—is hardly visible thanks to Apple’s display stack and clever use of a matte-finish nanotexture screen. The phone is IP68 dust- and water-resistant (though avoid taking the Duo to the beach, as sand is notoriously detrimental to phone hinges). The software experience, barring the unoptimized apps, feels carefully considered.
Apple has also landed on the right shape, months after Samsung realized it following seven years of narrow, somewhat awkward book-like folds . The wider, shorter “passport” design feels better than what’s come before in this category. The 5.4-inch outer screen is still big enough to be useful, and the hinge glides open gracefully and stays put at various angles. The hardware feels polished.
That’s not to say Apple has completely trounced the competition. I still appreciate that Samsung’s new Galaxy Z Fold8 is super lightweight at 201 grams, as the iPhone Duo’s hefty 254 grams (heavier than an iPhone 18 Pro Max ) can get tiring after extended doomscrolling. I don’t love the fact that, when closed, one side of the Duo has angled corners and the other is curved—the Fold8 looks better in that regard. Touch ID also takes a little getting used to after years of relying on Face ID, mostly when you’re holding the Duo with your left hand and you suddenly have to authenticate an app or purchase with your right hand. (It can mercifully auto-unlock if you’re wearing an Apple Watch .)
Apple also tightly controls the multitasking experience. If you have two apps split-screen on the Duo, Apple won’t let you resize one app to be slightly bigger than the other like you can on Android. Here, a 50-50 split is always enforced. You can’t add a floating third app when in split-screen either, even though Apple has offered a similar capability on iPads for years. (The exception is video apps—you can have them float in picture-in-picture mode.) In portrait orientation, you can split-screen only with a video app; Apple won’t let you stack two apps, something Android has enabled for years.
That rigid software philosophy extends to basic input handling, too. I am typing this review on the iPhone Duo using a compact folding keyboard with a tiny attached trackpad. The trackpad works OK, but I could only get it to work after turning on AssistiveTouch in iOS’ accessibility settings. If the Duo is the iPhone that lets you do more, Apple should natively enable cursor support just like it does on iPads .
Then there are the physical quirks. The Duo supports MagSafe , so you can magnetically stick the phone to MagSafe tripods, mounts, and the like . (When it’s open, the Duo’s weight makes the phone sag to one side.) But what about MagSafe wallets ? They’ll work, but Apple’s official wallet sticks out past the phone’s lower edge—not what you’d expect from a company that pores over every detail. Apple doesn’t have an official solution, so you’ll have to rely on a third-party accessory (and I suspect there will be many Duo accessories).
The iPhone maker follows the industry standard with a dual rear-camera system, lacking the third zoom camera from its Pro iPhones, which I sorely miss. At least the selfie cameras—the one on the outer screen and the “hidden” under-display inner camera seem to produce good results. On a Zoom call, my editor remarked that the video quality looked “really good” with both selfie shooters. (Zoom, by the way, wasn’t optimized.)
When an app is properly optimized, the experience is chef’s kiss . Multi-pane views let you see a lot more in an app than candy-bar phones, a boost to productivity. Split-screening two optimized apps looks excellent, with plenty of room for each app to breathe and let you multitask. I haven’t found myself putting the Duo in angled positions much, mostly because I’ve really enjoyed using it with Apple’s Folio With Kickstand case, so much so that I wish the kickstand were integrated into the phone itself; I strongly recommend investing in an accessory to prop the Duo up.
Battery life has been pretty great. With average use, I’ve ended most days with around 40 percent left by bedtime. Right now, with over six hours of screen-on time because I’ve been working off the Duo for most of the workday, it’s almost 6 pm, and I’m at 45 percent. Impressive.
As for performance, the only thing I've noticed is the Duo can get toasty. This isn't necessarily tied to a demanding task, though. Half an hour in Battlefleet Duo or Pokémon Go didn't make the phone feel much warmer (though 15 minutes in Ungodly did ), but at random moments, the right half of the Duo heated up quickly. It's something to keep an eye on.
Duo Preview lets the photo subject see themselves in the frame.
The dual rear cameras are reliable, too. You don’t get the fun variable-aperture wizardry of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera, but after comparing photos I’ve captured on both devices, the results aren’t drastically different. That brings us to the features I think will help bring folding phones into mainstream appeal—Smart Take and Duo Preview.
The latter is a staple of folding phones, letting you show the camera’s viewfinder to the photo subject—good news for anyone who has ever complained about their Instagram husband. Now you can make sure they’re angling the camera just right before hitting the shutter button. You can also take better-quality selfies with the rear camera yourself— open the camera app on the larger screen and flip the phone; you’ll get an option to view the camera controls on the outer screen, letting you see a live preview while snapping with the superior 48-megapixel cameras.
Smart Take is similar to Google’s Magic Capture . Set the phone down in a partially folded shape (so it looks like a tiny laptop) and tap the shutter button. The camera will then wait for you to get into position and snap a series of photos when it thinks you’re posing. You can forget about asking someone to take a picture for you. It’s not as smart as the Pixel feature —I ended up deleting a bunch of awkward Smart Take photos—but it’s convenient.
I’m sure Kids Cue will be popular too. I don’t have a kid, so I couldn’t vet how well it works, but it loops cute Snoopy animations on the outer display to capture a child’s attention and make them smile. Google and Samsung have similar versions on their folding phones,

articles.title_orig: Data center real estate is getting hard to find
articles.title_zh: Data center real estate is getting hard to find
articles.content_orig:
Demand for data center capacity is rewriting the rules of site selection. With interconnection queues stretching for years, power has become the scarcest input, and properties once discounted because of known or suspected contamination can offer infrastructure support that greenfield sites often cannot. This includes large tracts of industrially zoned land that already have transmission, substations, water, and transportation access. Additionally, federal, state, and local funding and tax benefits may be available to encourage development of these brownfield sites. For many developers, the question is no longer whether to consider a brownfield, but how to do it without inheriting its problems.
The federal government is encouraging this shift in perspective and practice. Executive Order 14318, Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure , directed the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to identify brownfield and Superfund sites that could support data center projects. Following issuance of its Guidance on the Redevelopment of Superfund and Brownfield Sites as AI Data Centers in January 2026, EPA has expanded its mapping tools to screen Superfund sites and large brownfields with potential for data center reuse. These projects are already happening. On its website , EPA highlights a data center built on two former textile and manufacturing brownfields in North Carolina, supported in part by EPA funds for brownfield activities. In California, a developer converted a former semiconductor manufacturing Superfund site into a data center after years of groundwater remediation.
But a contaminated site that looks attractive on a map is not necessarily ready to build on. Developers face two questions that must be answered together. The first is familiar: “Can we acquire this property without inheriting strict and potentially joint and several liability for historical contamination?” The second is just as important: “Can the existing contamination, remedy, and regulatory obligations coexist with the project we intend to build, on our schedule, and without jeopardizing liability protections?” A strong defense against liability on a site that cannot be developed on time is only half a solution, and so is a workable site plan that leaves the owner exposed. Both questions should shape diligence from the outset.
The sections below address each question in turn—how to secure and preserve liability protection, how to align the project with site conditions and the remedy, and how state and other federal environmental requirements fit into the picture.
1. Get the CERCLA Liability Protection Right Before Closing
CERCLA allows a buyer to acquire contaminated property and avoid owner or operator liability for existing contamination if it qualifies as a bona fide prospective purchaser (BFPP) or certain other defenses. Before acquisition, the buyer must conduct “all appropriate inquiries” (AAI) and have no disqualifying affiliation with a liable party. The protection is self-implementing in that EPA does not certify BFPP status, so the buyer must be able to prove every element if their invocation of statutory liability protections is ever challenged. In practice, the defense may be lost on technicalities that could have been avoided or fixed, including the following:
2. BFPP Duties Do Not End at Closing
Many mistakenly assume that liability protections are secured when the Phase I report is executed, but those efforts can be wiped out by post-closing inaction. After closing, a BFPP must take reasonable steps regarding existing releases of hazardous substances (e.g., prevent migration or exacerbation), comply with land use restrictions, not impede institutional controls, cooperate with and provide access to response personnel, respond to information requests, and provide required notices. It must also show that no disposal of hazardous substances occurred after it acquired the property, a requirement EPA addressed in its 2019 update to the Common Elements Guidance .
Construction is often when these obligations are tested. Moving thousands of cubic yards of soil, trenching through impacted areas, removing pavement that functions as impervious barriers, or relocating parts of an existing remedy can all implicate continuing obligations. Notably, in PCS Nitrogen Inc. v. Ashley II of Charleston , 714 F.3d 161 (4th Cir. 2013), a redeveloper that had performed AAI lost the defense because it failed to fill or cap sumps when it demolished structures and failed to address a debris pile. The practical lesson is that BFPP strategy and construction strategy must be developed together. Reasonable steps planning belongs in the demolition and grading scopes of work and the construction contracts, not just in the closing file.
3. CERCLA Liability Is Only One Layer
A BFPP analysis only addresses a CERCLA protection. Several other regimes can drive cost and schedule on a data center site, and some fall entirely outside the BFPP protection, including:
4. The State Program May Matter as Much as CERCLA
Most contaminated property transactions are resolved outside the federal Superfund program. State voluntary cleanup, brownfield, and corrective action programs often set the practical cleanup endpoint and can provide risk-based standards, liability protections, institutional control mechanisms, and “no further action” (NFA) or closure determinations that lenders expect. EPA’s guidance itself flags the importance of state NFA documentation for brownfields. Many states have voluntary cleanup programs that, on successful completion of the work, offer the incentive of a certificate or other documentation providing limited immunity from enforcement actions by the state (and from EPA under certain conditions).
However, these programs may involve tradeoffs that need to be carefully considered. State oversight can expand investigation and extend timelines, and state closure may not resolve federal Superfund liability, despite the CERCLA Section 128(b) enforcement bar. The presence of PCBs may complicate state oversight and require EPA involvement. A buyer that preserves BFPP status perfectly but learns after closing that the state will require years of additional investigation or remediation before excavation in the footprint has solved only part of the problem.
5. Design the Project and the Remedy Together
A legally compliant Phase I report assists in protecting against legacy liability, but it is not a development plan. It does not tell a developer the cost of building around contamination, or how to design or perform that work. It leaves open many more granular questions. Where will foundations, substations, utility corridors, stormwater facilities, and access roads go? Will excavation encounter impacted soil, or dewatering encounter contaminated groundwater? What needs to be done to prevent additional releases or migration of existing contamination to other properties? Does a planned building sit on a cap? Do monitoring wells or extraction systems cross the footprint? Will institutional controls accommodate future campus phases? A Phase II environmental site assessment can answer some of these questions, and potentially also set a baseline for future claims. As the site plan matures, the investigation should become development-specific.
At contaminated sites, developers often ask when the cleanup will be “finished.” That is usually the wrong question, as long-term monitoring and other requirements for some cleanups can span many years, if not decades. A remedy can be compatible with redevelopment long before cleanup levels are achieved, and EPA distinguishes physical completion of remedial construction from final attainment of cleanup goals. The better question is whether the intended use can coexist with the remedy. articles.title_orig: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
articles.title_zh: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is set to publicly file its S-1 investor prospectus as soon as Friday, according to three people familiar with the artificial intelligence firm's plans. The move would mark a crucial next step for what could be the biggest IPO in history.
The much-anticipated public debut , expected to surpass SpaceX's ( SPCX ) June IPO, is widely viewed as a crucial test of investor appetite for the artificial intelligence boom, as investors have become more concerned about the industry's massive spending.
Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft IPO registration statement to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in June. Under SEC rules, companies using the confidential process must make their registration materials available 15 calendar days before the start of their formal investor roadshow.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment on the timing of its S-1.
A public filing would clear a key procedural hurdle toward a potential November listing, though the timing of the offering remains subject to market conditions and other factors. Crucially, it would also give regular investors their first look at the financial details and risks around one of the AI industry's fastest-growing companies.
Anthropic is spending billions on AI infrastructure to train and run its suite of Claude models. That includes working with Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), as well as renting out graphics processor unit (GPU) capacity from SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center.
The company pulled in $16.3 billion in revenue over the first six months of 2026 and reported a net loss of over $80 billion, according to a Tuesday Wall Street Journal report . Wall Street is anticipating that the company could raise as much as $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters previously reported .
Last week, Anthropic told investors at its San Francisco office that its revenue climbed to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up from $11.5 billion in the second quarter, according to the Financial Times , noting that the company is also profitable on an adjusted basis.
The colossal offering comes as this year's banner IPO market is becoming more challenging. Earlier this week, shares of South Korean data center provider Elice plummeted a staggering 32% during its first trading day after raising $151 million. Nvidia-backed Firmus Grid abruptly shelved plans for a public listing earlier this month after investors balked at its proposed valuation, while several other companies have postponed plans to go public, citing market conditions.
Publicly traded AI-related companies have also waffled in recent days as investors become more selective over the industry's enormous spending needs. CoreWeave, in particular, has come under sharp scrutiny as investors question its future revenue prospects relative to its debt load.
The shift highlights how investors who enthusiastically bid up AI-related companies earlier this year have become more selective.
Given its enormous size, the timing of Anthropic's IPO is also expected to be a significant factor for other companies seeking to go public in the coming weeks, one person said.
CEO Dario Amodei co-founded Anthropic with his sister Daniela, the company's president.
Anthropic established a strong foothold in the enterprise market with its Claude chatbot, the popular AI coding tool Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.
Rival OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), which was initially expected to launch its IPO this year, is now projected to hit the public markets in early 2027.

articles.title_orig: NY congressional nominee Brad Lander says he was detained by the IDF in the West Bank
articles.title_zh: NY congressional nominee Brad Lander says he was detained by the IDF in the West Bank
articles.content_orig:
Lefty congressional nominee Brad Lander claimed Wednesday he was “detained” by the Israeli Defense Forces while working on an olive harvest in the West Bank.
Lander, the former Big Apple Comptroller who is running for Congress in the Nov. 3 election, posted a picture of himself glaring at the camera while onboard a bus with others who were on their phones and didn’t seem fazed.
“I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers,” Lander posted on X. “We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank.”
It is unclear if Lander, who is vying for New York’s 10th Congressional District seat, was doing anything else besides olive harvesting.
“The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know,” he added.
Lander had bested outgoing Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY) in their June primary, mounting a challenge against him from the left. Lander, who is Jewish, has been an outspoken critic of Israel.
During his primary against Goldman and his unsuccessful run for mayor last year, Lander made Israel a top issue.
The Dem candidate has opposed unconditional military aid to the Jewish state and accused it of carrying out a genocide in the Gaza Strip after the bloody Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack.
“I think — with deep sadness — that Israel’s conduct in Gaza meets the definition of genocide. But even if you don’t, it’s profoundly inconsistent with the Jewish value that every one of those Palestinian kids were created in the image of God, just like ours,” he posted on X in June.
Lander also contended that “Israel can’t be a genuine democracy while it’s occupying the West Bank & Gaza.”
Rabbis for Human Rights, an Israeli human rights group, corroborated Lander’s claim about being detained and said 90 other volunteers were held by the IDF as well, while harvesting olives in Nahalin, outside Bethlehem.
Authorities designated the area they were working in as a military zone closed for a full day, according to the group.
Officials then checked the group for identification, despite the group’s leaders offering to leave voluntarily, according to Rabbis for Human Rights’ version of events.
“We came to accompany farmers to land they have not been able to reach in three years, and after two hours of quiet harvesting, large forces arrived and closed the area,” Acting executive director for Rabbis for Human Rights, Anton Goodman, said in a statement.
“No one could have known about this order in advance. Instead of protecting people working their own land, the army is removing them from it, and detaining those who came to stand beside them.”
Lander previously described his venture to the West Bank as a mission to help Palestinians with their harvest and to put the spotlight on conditions there.
Other lefty pols have had similar run-ins with Israeli authorities. In July, for example, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) said he and his group were detained by the Israelis for over an hour while in the Palestinian village of Khirbet Zanuta during a tour.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Projects The Next Xbox May Cost $1,200 To $1,800, Says Report
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Projects The Next Xbox May Cost $1,200 To $1,800, Says Report
articles.content_orig:
We haven’t heard many details about Microsoft’s upcoming “Project Helix” gaming hardware since the company announced it in March as a device that will “play your Xbox and PC games.” In a new wide-ranging profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma , though, Fortune alludes to a dual release strategy for upcoming Microsoft gaming hardware, with “a next-generation handheld device” planned by the end of next year and a 2028 holiday season console release that could cost between $1,200 and $1,800.
That future console price range is based on what has “internally been projected” at the company, according to Fortune. But the price for consumers could come down if “Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost,” the outlet says, as many console makers have done in the past .
While a $1,200 starting price would be historically high for the game console market, even accounting for inflation , it also reflects a new normal: The slowdown in Moore’s Law and AI-driven component shortages means cutting-edge gaming hardware just isn’t as cheap as it used to be. This year, the Steam Machine broke the $1,000 starting price , while the 2-year-old technology in the PlayStation 5 Pro is now going for $900 , and the 6-year-old Xbox Series X now starts at $750 .
Fortune also reports that Microsoft is beset by internal clashes over whether its upcoming Helix handheld will run a “trimmed-down version of Windows Home”—akin to last year’s ROG Xbox Ally —or a bespoke operating system built and controlled by the Xbox group. Fortune cites “people briefed on the clash” in reporting that one high-level executive threatened to cancel the handheld altogether if they were forced to use Windows.
That threat seemingly helped lead to the current situation with the Xbox team “now largely controlling the direction of the operating system for the project, Fortune writes, though Sharma said the two groups are still working closely together. Fortune also reports that Microsoft has pressured the hardware team to move up the timelines for Project Helix hardware “by at least several months,” in part by using AI tools where applicable.
The profile also cites “people familiar with the strategy” in reporting that Xbox Game Pass will soon shift to a heavily tiered “a la carte” structure that lets subscribers pick and choose “add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer.” That would be an interesting shift from the current Game Pass plans, which all include some level of cloud-based gaming, console exclusives, and console multiplayer even for players who don’t make use of them.
Elsewhere in the wide-ranging profile, Fortune addresses concerns from “several current and former staff members” that Sharma was put in place merely to enact painful cuts before an impending sale of a spinoff of the Xbox group. But the piece also quotes Microsoft executive Judson Althoff pushing back against that idea, saying, “We would not have put [Sharma] on a business we intend to sell. There’s going to be a ton of speculation about all this. Time will tell.”

articles.title_orig: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are dominating the AI stock boom. Here's their edge
articles.title_zh: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are dominating the AI stock boom. Here's their edge
articles.content_orig:
In the United States, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley collectively generated about $52 billion in equity trading revenue this year. This is nearly 80% of the $67 billion that the five largest investment banks earned from equity operations as of September 30, CNBC reports .
The total revenue of the five largest banks from equity operations has already exceeded the result for all of 2025, which was a record year for this group, by $7 billion. Growth was driven by more active trading in stocks, ETFs and derivatives by institutional and retail investors, as well as global enthusiasm around companies linked to artificial intelligence.
Prime brokerage became an important source of revenue. As part of this business, banks provide hedge funds with margin loans, securities lending services and other trading services. Bank executives reported growing demand for financing bets on AI equipment manufacturers, hyperscalers and chip suppliers.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram .
At Goldman Sachs, revenue from financing equity transactions rose 96% in the third quarter, to a record $3.37 billion. JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley do not disclose this figure separately, but said they saw similar dynamics.
The largest banks are able to conduct multibillion-dollar deals, including leveraged swaps on volatile shares of AI companies or sector ETFs. According to traders, such institutions can absorb potential losses of $100 million on an individual transaction without a significant impact on quarterly results. Smaller or more specialized banks may therefore turn down some deals.
Institutional investors also actively invested in South Korea and Taiwan, focusing on manufacturers of memory chips and semiconductors for data center construction. At the same time, the International Monetary Fund warned that rising leverage, crowded positions and correlated asset sales by hedge funds could create risks to financial stability. The IMF estimated global hedge fund assets at $13 trillion.

articles.title_orig: After A Year Of Layoffs, Disney Finds $180 Million For Recruits From Bankrupt Character.AI
articles.title_zh: After A Year Of Layoffs, Disney Finds $180 Million For Recruits From Bankrupt Character.AI
articles.content_orig:
Sign up to get our news digest — delivered directly to your inbox twice a week.
Disney has spent much of 2026 cutting jobs and announcing restrictions on employee benefits, with the reductions continuing under new CEO Josh D’Amaro. Now, it plans to spend roughly $180 million over three years to compensate and retain 66 recruits from the recently bankrupt, highly controversial chatbot startup Character.AI.
According to Business Insider , citing bankruptcy filings, the hiring follows September layoffs that included technology workers. The recruits are following former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand, whom Disney recently appointed its first company-wide chief technology officer. The group crossing over constitutes most of Character.AI’s approximately 86-person workforce at September’s end.
As we reported last week , Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 protection on October 12, ten days after Anand officially joined Disney. Disney separately offered $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to certain intellectual property and certain company claims, subject to the bankruptcy sale process.
The spending adds another revealing chapter to Disney’s year of restructuring and continued efforts to get ahead in the AI race. The company eliminated jobs in January, approximately 1,000 more in April, and hundreds in July, including roughly 150 at Pixar .
In September, Disney’s top lawyer warned employees that his department would shrink substantially as the company considered automation, outside providers, and outsourcing. Beginning in 2027, Disney will also restrict spousal health coverage when spouses can obtain insurance through their own employers, even if those plans offer worse benefits.
These decisions come alongside substantial profits and shareholder payouts. Disney reported $5.6 billion in fiscal third-quarter segment operating income, up 21%, and raised its fiscal-year share-buyback target to at least $9 billion.
Big picture, the layoffs, benefit restrictions, buybacks, and AI hiring reveal consistent spending priorities. Disney is willing to commit substantial sums to AI expertise (remember its proposed $1 billion investment in OpenAI, announced alongside a Sora licensing deal that collapsed just over three months later, before any money changed hands?) and shareholder returns, while asking its existing workforce to absorb repeated cuts.

Xbox Ally and Xbox Series X |S consoles are about to get a big AMD -shaped boost.
Yesterday, AMD and Microsoft revealed that FSR 4.1 is coming to the entire suite of current-gen Xbox devices . That includes Xbox Ally (base model), Xbox Ally X, and Xbox Series X|S consoles.
FSR 4.1 is an upscaling technology that allows games to render images at a lower resolution, passing overhead to performance. Then, FSR 4.1 upscales the image to create a sharper image, granting the appearance of higher native resolution. Technologies like FSR and DLSS have been boosting the lifespan of older and less-powerful hardware for some time now, and given the on-going RAMpocalypse and component crisis, anything that extends the usability of more affordable hardware is a win in my book.
But, when can we expect to get our hands (and eyes) on it? Here's what our sources are telling us so far.
FSR 4.1 will become available to Xbox Series X|S game developers in the next couple of weeks . Some partner developers have already had early access in preview builds, and will enable FSR 4.1 earlier than others. In the AMD video above, the firm used Blood of Dawnwalker to demonstrates FSR 4.1 boosts on Xbox Ally devices, so you can probably expect that to be among the first batch.
For Xbox Ally X and the Xbox Ally base model, AMD and ASUS will ship updated drives to the Armoury Crate's new "Preview Update" segment by Friday, Oct 23. The new preview segment which lets users test out early builds if they don't mind risking some bugs and polish, similar to the Xbox and Windows Insider programs.
Developers that have enabled FSR 4.1 on existing PC games will automatically get enhanced when the drivers go live on Xbox Ally devices.
On Xbox Series X|S console, FSR 4.1 won't be retroactively injected into existing games. Developers will have to implement it into their existing games via updates , or support it out of the box in future games.
Sources tell me that there is a "handful" of FSR 4.1-enhanced titles slated for the holiday season on Xbox Series X|S, with a steady feed of new games gaining FSR 4.1 throughout 2027 and beyond.
FSR 4.1 should provide a meaningful quality bump for all sorts of games across Xbox Series X|S and Xbox Ally X and the base model, but perhaps more so on the lower-end devices. The Xbox Series S has been notorious for performance trade offs, with developers struggling with the irregular RAM allocation.
Games on Xbox Series X|S that presently trade resolution down for frame rates should get noticeably sharper even in performance mode when implemented.
People have been using apps like Optiscaler on Github to inject FSR 4 on devices like the Steam Deck , and the results have been impressive, but setting it up can be a chore. Native, official support should bring a ton of performance benefits for the Xbox range across the board without the headaches of using workarounds.
As soon as it's available, I'll be demonstrating how it all works in practice right here on Windows Central.
The big question is ... will GTA 6 support it? Time will tell.

European leaders are talking a big game on China, but will avoid a full-blown trade war due to internal division and fear of retaliation: analysts
The European Union is likely to avoid a full-blown trade confrontation with China due to internal divisions in the bloc and fear of retaliation, according to a prominent research firm.
But the bloc would “continue to pull its punches” in any confrontation with Beijing due to a lack of consensus among and within Europe’s member states, the London-based Capital Economics said at an event in Hong Kong on Wednesday.
The EU also had “concerns over retaliation” if it stepped up trade tensions with China, the research firm said, and held “lingering hopes to save the rules-based global trading system” that had helped Europe in the past.

articles.title_zh: North Korea tells border troops to take ‘resolute action’ if South threatens their safety
articles.content_orig:
North Korea has told its border troops to take “prompt ​and resolute action” if South Korean forces threaten their safety, state media ​said on Wednesday, raising the risk of a clash along the ⁠heavily armed frontier.
The report came a day after Seoul pledged to punish “resolutely” any ​further provocation by Pyongyang if North Korea acted on threats to strengthen its military ​posture along the border.
North Korean Army Marshal Pak Jong Chon inspected fortifications on the border with South Korea on Tuesday, accompanied by Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong ​Un, KCNA reported.
Kim Yo Jong said new firepower units had “taken their firing positions” at ​the border, KCNA reported.
Tensions between North and South Korea have risen since Pyongyang began fortifying its ‌border ⁠in April 2024. The two countries are separated by the Demilitarized Zone that was established when the Korean War ended in an armistice in 1953.
Seoul says Pyongyang has sent up to 7,000 workers to the border this year, with about 50 ​crossings of the ​Military Demarcation Line, ⁠which bisects the DMZ, to South Korea’s side of the border.
These North Korean brothers spent 10 years planning their escape. Months after reaching freedom, everything changed
On Wednesday, North Korea rejected Seoul’s allegations, with Pak dismissing ​the claim as an “absurd assertion” designed to shift blame, KCNA reported.
The ​North Korean ⁠army knew where the border lay “better than any others” and was only doing what it should within its own territory, Pak said, urging soldiers to turn the border ⁠into an “impregnable ​fortress.”
South Korea said North Korean mines caused ​a border blast last month that seriously wounded two of its soldiers, and called on Pyongyang to suspend the ​fortification work.

articles.title_orig: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.title_zh: PHP2Shell: What Actually Protects You Before the 14:00 UTC PHP RCE Patch, and What Doesn't
articles.content_orig:
You cannot fully block the two critical PHP flaws called PHP2Shell before today's fix, and the one setting being passed around as a workaround is not enough on its own, the security firm that suggested it now says.
PHP will release the fix at 14:00 UTC on October 21 for two flaws it rates 9.2 out of 10, and has given no workaround of its own. Until you can install it, what lowers your risk is taking exposed PHP off the internet or behind access controls, cutting what a compromised server can reach, and having the update ready to apply the moment it lands.
Cloudflare says it is seeing early attempts to exploit the flaws, and has pushed emergency rules for sites behind it that it calls a stopgap until you patch. No compromise has been confirmed, the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work, and neither flaw is in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws. PHP has not said which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, or whether any setting changes the risk; it says the full details and the fixed versions come with the release.
At the time of writing, that release was not yet out. So nobody outside the group that found the flaws can test whether a given defense works, which is why the advice below is about lowering risk, not promising safety.
The workaround spreading on social media and security blogs is one line in a PHP configuration file: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 . It turns off Session Upload Progress, a PHP feature that's enabled by default, which records how far a file upload has progressed so another request can check on it.
GMO Flatt Security, a Tokyo security firm, suggested setting it early on October 21, saying it could not be sure the change fully addresses the flaws but thought it would help with some probability.
Later the same day, the firm walked that back. In an update timestamped 14:00 Japan time (05:00 UTC), it said the setting alone is not a complete fix and that attacks getting around it are expected. It told administrators to prepare their update, watch for attack traffic before the release, and apply the fix as soon as it is out.
Two people from the PHP project said the same thing more bluntly. Replying to someone who suggested the upload-progress setting might patch the flaw, Gina Peter Banyard, a PHP core developer and documentation writer funded by the PHP Foundation, wrote : "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP. I sadly know too much." Joe Ferguson, the release manager for the coming PHP 8.6, put it shorter : "ini settings won't save you."
The setting cannot be relied on for two reasons. GMO Flatt expects a way around it but has not said what that is. And the whole idea that the flaw lives in Session Upload Progress is a guess: PHP has not confirmed it, the firm itself said it holds only so far as its own research matches PHP2Shell, and an independent code audit argues the specific bug others describe in that feature does not exist in released PHP. That audit is from an anonymous account and PHP's own code will settle it, but it is one more reason not to treat the setting as a shield.
Not everyone agrees. One vendor, Upwind, still lists the setting as an immediate mitigation , passing along another researcher's analysis rather than its own tests. watchTowr, which reproduced one of the flaws, says there is "no confirmed patch or workaround at this time."
No one is telling you to undo the change. The instruction is only not to count it as protection. PHP's own manual already advises turning the feature off where an application does not use upload progress bars, because the stored file names and field names "are not validated and may contain PHP code." If you turned it on by mistake somewhere that needs it, the only cost is that upload progress bars stop working.
Check that the change is actually in effect on the process that serves web traffic, not on the command line. The setting is INI_PERDIR, so it can be set in php.ini, .htaccess, or .user.ini.
A .user.ini file is read only by the CGI and FastCGI versions of PHP, not by the Apache module, and PHP re-reads it only every 300 seconds by default, so a change there can take five minutes to apply.
Under the Apache module, use .htaccess or the server config. Confirm the value on PHP-FPM or mod_php, whichever serves your site, not on php -i at the shell.
Get ready now. GMO Flatt's advice is to confirm your update steps and the checks you run afterward, rehearse any config change, and line up the people and approvals for a possible emergency restart. When the fix lands, update the runtime that serves web requests, which is PHP-FPM, mod_php, or CGI, not the application on top of it.
PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches, 8.2 through 8.5. Which exact versions carry the fix and how far back the flaws extend will be announced with the release.
The Hacker News reported the branch support and the wider background in its earlier coverage of the disclosure.
Where an immediate update is not possible, CERT-EU advises organizations to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied." Banyard put the same point from inside the project: turning a server off for a day "might be the most sensible thing to do. But that is far from a reasonable thing to demand for most people." Short of shutting down, restrict reach: put the site behind a VPN, allowlisted clients, or authenticated access at the edge, and check that traffic cannot reach the origin directly around those controls.
Shrink what an attacker gets if the server is taken over. GMO Flatt's other steps are to reduce the data stored on the server, reduce its privileges, remove stored credentials, including cloud roles, and ensure logging is enabled and kept in a secure location so you can investigate later.
Branches older than 8.2, including 8.1, 7.x, and 5.x, are end-of-life and receive no PHP fixes. For those, upgrade, take the system offline, or isolate it; a Linux distribution or hosting provider may backport a fix on its own schedule.
A web application firewall is a stopgap here, not a fix, and Cloudflare says so itself. It has pushed emergency rules for the known exploit paths, free tier included, which its CTO calls "a STOPGAP only" ahead of patching. Such rules only see traffic that passes through Cloudflare, and they can miss new attack paths as they appear.
Updating WordPress, Laravel, or another application does not update the PHP runtime underneath it; that comes from your server package, host, or container image. On managed or shared hosting, ask your provider when a fixed PHP build will land and have them stand by.
Hosting providers build their packages only after PHP ships the fix: CloudLinux, for one, says its updated packages depend on the upstream release and will be posted when ready.
Exploitation is early and unconfirmed. Cloudflare reports emerging attempts; watchTowr says it reproduced one flaw but has not reported attacks; the public exploit code going around has not been shown to work; and neither flaw was in CISA's catalog of known exploited flaws when it was last checked on October 21.
A researcher has posted a video said to demonstrate the exploit chain, and the audit above states that the circulating proof-of-concept code does not fire against released PHP. Treat all of this as a snapshot that can change by the hour.
When the fix ships, check the fixed version for your branch, which versions PHP lists as affected, whether PHP confirms or rejects any setting as a mitigation, and whether the session code changed, which also answers the dispute over where the flaw lives.
The fixed versions and the advisory will appear on php.net and through PHP's GitHub security advisories , where the project assigns its own identifiers. After updating, review your logs for anything that happened before you patched.

President Donald Trump points as he speaks at a midterm campaign rally at Pitt-Greenville Airport in Greenville, N.C., on Tuesday. ( (Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Images)
President Donald Trump on Tuesday vowed to treat potential rioters in the U.S. “very rough,” pointing to the unrest that has gripped France in recent days.
Trump made the remarks during a speech in Greenville, North Carolina, ahead of the midterm elections, after a heckler interrupted him as he campaigned for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley.
“They're crazy, these people. Look at that guy. He's a nutjob,” Trump said, referring to the protester in the crowd.
Trump warned that he would crack down on potential threats, saying he would not allow similar unrest to take hold in the U.S.
“That's what you witness over the last three or four days. You watch nutjobs like him in France ruining their country,” Trump said. “We're not going to put up with it by the way.”
“If a possible threat, which could happen, I hope you won't get angry if I treat them very, very rough, because that's what's going to happen. They're not going to destroy our country.”
Click here to follow the latest updates with the protests in France.
Albanian police have clashed with anti-government protesters for an eighth consecutive day in the capital, Tirana , as demonstrators call for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, according to the Associated Press.
Similar to unrest sweeping across Europe, Albania’s protests have been fueled by discontent over rising fuel costs, the education system and a housing crisis, the AP said.
During the protests, demonstrators reportedly have hurled rocks, flares and firebombs at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.
Rama condemned the protests Tuesday, saying attempts to force political change through violence would never be allowed, according to the AP.
“A wave of stones, an attempt to overthrow the government and change those in power through the imposition of violence — something that will never be allowed to happen, in any form or for any reason,” Rama said Tuesday after a meeting with teachers and representatives of Tirana’s schools.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, attends the fifth session of the UN Permanent Forum on People of African Descent. Türk condemned violence and vandalism during protests across Europe while urging police to avoid excessive force. (Getty Images)
UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk on Tuesday condemned riots that have erupted across Europe over rising living costs, urging police to respond lawfully and calling for accountability for protesters who commit acts of violence and vandalism.
“I deplore the actions of those exploiting protests to commit acts of violence and vandalism against public and private property. They should be held individually accountable,” Turk said.
“I am concerned by reports of unnecessary and excessive use of force against protesters, including children. States must ensure that any law enforcement response remains lawful, necessary and proportionate. Allegations of unlawful use of force must be investigated promptly, effectively and independently, with accountability and effective remedies for victims.”
Türk called for “inclusive and safe dialogue” between governments and protesters to prioritize human rights concerns .
“I further urge States to engage protesters, particularly young people, in meaningful, inclusive and constructive dialogue, and to take concrete steps to address legitimate and fundamental human rights concerns over education, public services, housing, the rising cost of living and inequality,” he said.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni speaks during a joint statement in Rome on Jan. 23, 2026. (Remo Casilli/Reuters)
Italy on Tuesday announced a series of tougher security measures following reports of looting and vandalism that rocked Milan and other cities over the weekend.
The measures include deploying 500 additional military personnel in Milan, requiring offenders or their parents to pay for damaged property, and imposing harsher penalties on protesters who engage in violence.
The additional military personnel will work alongside law enforcement through the end of year, while the government plans to expand judicial resources to ensure legal consequences for offenders, including some teenagers.
Under the measures, minors or their parents would also be required to pay for property they damage, the council said.
“Of course, they can oppose it, but in the meantime, the parents of that boy who enjoyed smashing everything will have to pay. And whoever suffered the damage will be able to recover everything, from that family's assets, even from any money the state may owe them,” the council said in a release statement.
The council added that nearly 200 officers have been injured and property damage in Milan alone is estimated at around 1 million euros, citing Confcommercio, Italy’s largest business association.
Protesters set fire to the town hall in Limoges Haute-Vienne in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region of France on Oct. 17, 2026. (Elise Cabane / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images)
The U.S. Embassy in France is warning Americans to steer clear of violent protests as unrest sparked curfews and raised concerns about travel disruptions across the country.
The riots — fueled by a range of grievances, including rising living costs and mass migration — have been reported across France, with protests reported in cities including Paris, Lille and Lyon.
Authorities have imposed localized curfews as a result.
The embassy said in a Monday statement that partial curfews had been introduced in several French cities, with additional restrictions possible.
"Following the October 17 protests that turned violent, media report the Prime Minister’s office introduced partial curfews for Monday, October 19 and Tuesday, October 20 in several cities across France, including Lille," the embassy said.
"Media report more curfews may follow for parts of Paris and in prefectures across the country, and that scattered protests could continue."
This is an excerpt of an article by Fox News Digital's Andrea Margolis.
France's Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu leaves the Interior Ministry in Paris on October 19, 2026. (JULIEN DE ROSA / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Tuesday accused far-left groups of organizing “insurrectionary” plans linked to the riots that erupted over the weekend.
During a raucous parliamentary session, Lecornu blasted “the planning, in certain locations, of an insurrectionary plan led by far-left and ultra-left fringe groups,” according to the French National Assembly.
Lecornu said the riots were joined by criminals seeking to “loot and destroy” property, according to the French National Assembly.
"No one will impose their political agenda through violence,” he added.
"Peaceful demonstrations have their rightful place in our Republic. Arson, looting, and attacks have none," he said.
The violent protests over the cost of living in Paris have prompted French authorities to deploy military forces to reinforce police ahead of Saturday’s planned demonstrations , Reuters reported.
Trash burns during clashes between protestors and police officers during a demonstration against rising living costs, joining students' grievances, in Paris, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Emma Da Silva)
President Donald Trump on Tuesday dismissed concerns that a socialist agenda could spark unrest in the U.S. similar to riots in France, arguing that the two countries are fundamentally different.
Trump cited economic growth and his administration’s immigration crackdown as two key differences that sets the U.S. apart from its European counterpart.

articles.title_orig: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.title_zh: Putin, at talks with Witkoff, suggests he and Trump could meet in China
articles.content_orig:
United States Special Envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian leaders on the Ukraine war following “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway.
Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday in the city in northwestern Russia, as the US pushes for an end to the war that began more than four and a half years ago with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Zelenskyy in recent weeks and has suggested that someone else should negotiate on Kyiv’s behalf. The remarks signalled a new low in their relationship, while Zelenskyy has accused the US of suspending crucial intelligence sharing.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the talks between Witkoff and Zelenskyy as “positive”, adding that the US envoy would share the results with Putin. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also attended the talks with Zelenskyy, but did so virtually because of illness. Kushner is also expected to attend the meeting with Putin remotely.
“He’ll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side – and let’s see if we can make some progress,” Rubio said.
The prime ministers of Norway and Finland also attended the talks in Oslo. Representatives from the European Union and NATO were present. Following Tuesday’s talks, Zelenskyy said “very, very important” intelligence from the US had been restored.
Zelenskyy has also accused Washington of slowing down the internet service, Starshield, which is crucial for Ukraine’s battlefield operations. Starshield is the military-grade equivalent of Starlink and is also developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Rubio dismissed Zelenskyy’s accusations, saying Trump had “nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield”. Musk disputes this and says such decisions can only be made by the US military and president.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk ordered the slowdown of the service, citing US officials and people familiar ⁠with the matter.
As diplomatic efforts intensify, Russia and Ukraine continue to trade long-range attacks.
At least one person was killed and two were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack in Russia’s western Bryansk ⁠region on Wednesday, Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said on Telegram.
The Ukrainian Emergency Service said two people were killed in a Russian attack on a high-rise building in the Sviatoshinsky district of the capital, Kyiv.
